mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST declines for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% interacts with a concurrent decline in consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS falling for two months) to signal aggressive tightening amid weakening demand, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND RSAFS declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS jumps above 4.5% and RSAFS falls for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA +10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month MA by more than 10% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal often preceding major labor market rebalancing; when observed together for two months, it foreshadows a subsequent negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days due to uncertainty and wage inflation risks.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for five consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA +2% for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA by more than 2% for five consecutive months.
